category_title: Middle school students with diverse learning disorders and low reading engagement
minimal_context: The student is working in a group to debate Greek gods and goddesses and create a storyboard for a play.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please get with your group. You need to debate about the Greek gods and goddesses, decide what attribute belonged to which god, and discuss what these gods and goddesses would really say in certain situations.

STUDENT: (Sits away from the peers, appearing typically withdrawn) I can't organize my thoughts or information for this.

TUTOR: Just try to talk to your group. It is part of the delicate process of creating a play.

STUDENT: (Becomes disruptive in class, struggling with the social situation) I don't want to talk to them. I have no motivation to do this.

TUTOR: Please look at the storyboard with detailed pictures of each scene and try your best.

STUDENT: (Pushes the mask and jewelry away, showing a complete lack of self-control and remaining withdrawn) No! I'm not doing it!

options.A: Allow the student to express unique talents by assigning specific roles, such as playing a powerful god, designing jewelry, or creating the storyboard.
options.B: Counter the student's arguments by pointing out the specific ways they have already demonstrated growth and change during the play creation process.
options.C: Understand the relationship between the student's disruptive 'fight' responses and anxiety, and frame them into positive coping strategies during group work.
options.D: Frame the student as a professional playwright; justify mundane tasks, like organizing storyboard scenes, by comparing them to professional theater standards.
